verdict: OK to lend in Muzaffarnagar sugar & ethanol, but only to integrated mills with distillery capacity and clean cane-payment records; avoid pure-standalone mills and any account with cane arrears or mill-area disputes.
title: Muzaffarnagar Sugar & Ethanol: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A mill buys cane from a fixed command area, crushes it into sugar, molasses and bagasse, and now increasingly diverts juice/grain to ethanol. **Cash comes from three taps: sugar sales, ethanol supplies, and power/co-gen** — and the ethanol tap is the steadiest because pricing is administered [10]. Cane is paid within a statutory window, so the mill carries a heavy seasonal working-capital peak from November crushing to sugar sales through the year. **The single biggest cash risk is cane arrears** — a mill that falls behind loses its farmers and its command area.

## Where value and cash sit now
Realisation is the swing factor: EID Parry lifted average realisation to INR 51.2 per kilogram from INR 43.7 per kilogram on a premium mix [6], and Triveni reported improved profitability and reduced debt on strong sugar and distillery margins [5]. **Integrated mills with distillery capacity are earning through the cycle; standalone mills are not.** Locally, farmers protested a change in the mill area [1] and staged a novel protest selling sugar at 45 rupees a kilo against higher prices [2] — read this as farmer and price sensitivity in the belt, not as a demand collapse. **Local sources say little about mill-level financials in Muzaffarnagar, so lean on first principles plus these peers.**

## What has changed
UP GST collections ran +14.2% Apr-to-date against India +6.1% [D] — a genuine local tailwind for consumption and trade. But India-wide bank credit is -7.0% YoY against output +5.1% [D], so **credit is scarce and your pricing should reflect that**. Rating commentary flags that remunerative ethanol prices and interest subvention on distillery capex help prevent cane arrears [10]; that support is the reason to stay with integrated borrowers.

## Who to pursue, and how to grow safely
Pursue integrated mills with operating distilleries, co-gen, and a clean cane-payment record; pursue ethanol-logistics and molasses-handling units tied to them. Avoid standalone mills with no ethanol diversion, and any borrower whose command area is under dispute [1]. **Structure against the crush cycle**: cash credit sized to the November-April peak, a term loan only where distillery capex is backed by subvention [10], and a cane-arrears covenant tested monthly. Take every month: cane payment status, sugar stock and sales register, ethanol dispatch and payment advices, and quarterly stock statements. When a proposal lands, check the mill-area notification and cane arrears first; if arrears exceed one fortnight, ask for the payment plan before sanction.

## Early-warning signs
- Cane arrears crossing the statutory window -> freeze fresh limits and inspect the command area.
- Farmer protests or mill-area changes [1] -> re-check cane supply assumptions.
- Sugar realisation slipping below peer levels [6] -> stress-test the ethanol share.
- Distillery downtime or ethanol payment delays [10] -> ask for dispatch records.
- Stock statement ageing beyond normal -> verify with a godown visit.
